ROOT CAUSE: removed_seqs (merge.rs) only treats an ancestor event as reverted if it sits ABOVE the branch's min-seq watermark (min(seq)-1); anything below is assumed folded into the baseline by compaction. So any revert that raises a branch's min seq above the reverted seq is invisible -- TWO triggers: (a) reverting the branch's EARLIEST event(s) (no compaction needed -- see the revert_below_the_watermark_is_not_yet_detected unit test), and (b) reverting an event and LATER compacting past it. In both, merging against a branch that still carries the event resurrects it, and the outcome depends on merge direction (breaking convergence). Trigger (a) needs no compaction at all, so it is more reachable than first thought; (b) is gated by keep_events. Currently silent. ACTION: at merge time we have ancestor + ours + theirs, so detect the ambiguous case (an ancestor event absent from one branch BELOW that branch's watermark while still present in the other branch's shared region, seq <= fork) and warn loudly instead of silently resurrecting/diverging -- same no-silent-failure approach as the seq-reuse warning in content_mismatches and the orphan warnings. Decide whether to only warn or also surface/fail the merge. Add an e2e repro that asserts the warning fires. Analysis and characterization tests are in task seq-gaps-revert (merge.rs).

RESOLUTION (won't implement): a sound log-only detector is infeasible. The shape it would key on -- an ancestor event absent from a branch BELOW that branch's min-seq watermark while still present in the other branch -- is ALSO produced by ordinary compaction when two branches fold to different depths (verified against the baseline_keep_ours_merges_after_both_branches_compact test: the boundary event is folded into one branch's baseline but kept live in the other's log). Telling a real revert from a compaction fold requires that branch's BASELINE (event present there = folded/safe; absent = reverted/dangerous), and the log merge driver is handed only the mutation logs (%O %A %B), never the baseline. A baseline-aware detector (git show MERGE_HEAD:.taska/baseline.jsonl etc.) would work but couples the pure log driver to git refs and the baseline and cripples the merge unit tests. Given the bug is rare (revert below the watermark AND a concurrent branch that kept the event), we accept and document it instead. Documented in CLAUDE.md invariants, the removed_seqs comment, and the revert_below_the_watermark_is_a_known_limitation test (all in merge.rs); the full prose write-up lives in protocol-doc.

edges in the `relationships` map like every other typed relationship, so engine.rs
and graph.rs stop special-casing the name. After this, `model::DEPENDS_ON` is used

the optimize-relationship-storage measurements.)

has a separate storage field:

  - graph::blocker_edges handles the dedicated field separately (membership + label).
Unify the storage and both special-cases disappear: apply_dep inserts every edge
into the map uniformly; blocker_edges just iterates the map and filters by the
passed-in blocker set.

  - engine::apply_dep: insert/remove ALL edges (incl. depends_on) in relationships,
    keyed by rel_type; drop the dedicated-field branch.
  - graph::blocker_edges: iterate relationships only; no depends_on branch/label.
  - Add an accessor deps(&TaskState) -> &[String] reading relationships[DEPENDS_ON],

    -- i.e. the string stays a parse/serialize concern.

byte-identical (covered by the output-consistency e2e test).

A write-time verification gate now exists (cli::vet_events, run atomically under
the store lock via EventStore::append_checked). It already enforces the STRUCTURAL
rules: reject duplicate create / mutation of a missing task / self-reference / dep
on a missing target / reserved+computed field names; drop no-ops; reject `+=` on
the single-valued status field. type-schemas should extend its PER-FIELD checks
(there's an explicit hook comment in vet_events). Deferred here:
  - Per-field VALUE types: priority is an int, a status is one of an allowed set,
    a date field is RFC3339, etc. Reject a value that doesn't match the field's
    declared type.
  - Which fields accept `+=` (append): generalize the ad-hoc status-field rejection
    — only text/list fields accept append; scalar/enum fields don't.
  - Allowed/required/unknown fields per task type (the store is schema-agnostic
    today): optionally reject undeclared fields and require mandatory ones.
  - Reserved/computed names are already blocked (cli::reserved_field_names); the
    schema layers on top.
NOT a type-schema concern, but raised during this work: write-time dependency-CYCLE
prevention. Current design deliberately ALLOWS cycles and reports them at read
(`ta list --ready`, `ta dep cycles`; tests encode this). Treat changing that as a
separate "dependency integrity" decision, not part of type-schemas.

After unifying depends_on into the relationships map, the `deps` column still shows
only depends_on() (relationships["depends_on"]). Make it show ALL of a task's
relationship edges, styled by kind. (Per the design discussion.)

DECISIONS (from the user):
  - `deps` shows ALL relationship edges (across every declared type), not just
    depends_on. (Correct for the default config either way — its only blocker is
    depends_on — but matters for multi-blocker / richly-typed configs.)
  - Table/human view: edges whose type GATES readiness (the blocker_types set:
    blocker + hierarchy kinds) render BOLD; informational (info-kind) edges render
    DIM. So you can see at a glance what blocks vs what's just related.

PLUMBING (the hard part — format is config-light today):
  - format::cell_value("deps") needs the relationship kinds to aggregate all
    targets (data) — thread a blocker/kind set (or RelationshipConfig) into the
    render path (render/render_rows/render_human/render_record + list.rs/show.rs
    callers). It currently has no config.
  - Per-target bold/dim can't go through emit_row's column-level coloring (it
    colors the whole padded cell uniformly). Build the deps cell with per-target
    SGR, compute width on the PLAIN (no-SGR) text so alignment stays exact, and
    skip column_sgr for deps. render_record needs the same.
  - JSON/jsonl: decide the deps array shape — flat array of all targets across
    types, vs keep it blocker-only and rely on `show` for the per-type breakdown.
    (No color in json regardless; covered by the output-consistency e2e test.)
  - Keep the `subtasks` column separate (hierarchy progress) even though hierarchy
    edges also gate — avoid implying deps replaces it.

Follow-up to scm-health-check (2026-06-06): health detection and `ta init` reuse already
support a .taska that lives BELOW the SCM root, but two code paths still assume the
store's parent IS the repo root:

     `git show HEAD:.taska/mutations.jsonl` — a ROOT-relative blob path, hardcoded.
     For a nested store it always fails -> committed count 0 -> undo treats committed
     events as local and TRUNCATES shared history instead of compensating. Fix: make
     the path repo-relative from the store dir (`git show HEAD:./<path>` with -C at
     the store parent resolves cwd-relative), or compute the prefix via
     `git rev-parse --show-prefix`. Note it also ignores configured [store] file names.

     silently uses the DEFAULT on_conflict policy and writes no conflict marker. The
     driver already receives %P (the repo-relative path of the file being merged,
     currently bound as `path: _`) — derive the store dir from it instead of discovery.

fine; setup's .gitattributes at the store parent is correct by gitattributes scoping).

    an enum over the declared type names. Unsetting (null) a required field rejected.

DECISION (user, 2026-06-06): numeric += and -= make sense; generalize append.

    int/uint/float fields, element PUSH on array<T> fields; rejected on bool/enum.
  - -=: numbers only — sugar for adding the negated operand; rejected elsewhere.
HEADLINE DESIGN DECISION (recorded recommendation, confirm at impl start):
  - Recommended: a NEW OpType::Add carrying the numeric delta. Append's replay
    semantics stay untouched (retrofitting number-sniffing into Append would change
    how EXISTING logs materialize across versions — a replay-semantics break).
    Add commutes on merge like Append (concurrent +=2 / +=3 converge either order).
    -= parses to Add with a negated operand — no third op. Cost: an addition to the
    on-disk op contract (old binaries can't read logs containing it; forward-compat
    only — document in protocol-doc, note in release notes).
  - Alternative (rejected unless strong reason): overload Append with type-sniffing
    at replay — no new op, but retroactively changes old-log materialization.
  - Array push: could reuse Append for array fields (apply_append branches on the
    CURRENT value being an array)? Same retroactivity concern applies — decide
    alongside the Add decision.

notes:
GOAL: make `ta undo` intuitive and more powerful. Today it is confusing: running undo a SECOND time just undoes the previous undo (committed undo appends compensating events, so the next undo targets those). The intuitive expectation is that repeated `ta undo` keeps walking BACK through the real history - undoing successively older ORIGINAL events and skipping anything already undone.

CHANGES:
1. UNDO MARKER: every undo (compensating) event carries `_undoes=<seq>` naming the original event it reverses. An original event is "already undone" iff some event carries `_undoes=<that seq>`. Decide the marker's home: `_meta` already holds non-materialized merge provenance, so a sibling there fits; it must NOT reach task state, and must be added to the RESERVED keys.
2. REPEATED undo walks back: `ta undo` (no args) selects the most recent ORIGINAL event that is (a) not itself an undo-marker event and (b) not already undone, then undoes it. Calling undo N times peels back N genuine events, never bouncing on its own undos.
3. `--seq <SEQ>`: undo the specific event at SEQ.
4. `--seq <SEQ> --count N`: start at SEQ and undo N events going backward (older), skipping already-undone events along the way.
5. SKIP already-undone: whenever selecting events (--count, --seq, --seq+--count), skip any whose seq already has an `_undoes` pointing at it.

KEEP the append-only invariant: undoing uncommitted (local) events may still truncate; undoing committed events appends compensating events carrying `_undoes`. (Revisit: always appending markers - even for uncommitted - may make repeated-undo + the skip-set uniform and simpler than truncation; decide.)

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Exact home + spelling of the marker (`_undoes` in the envelope vs under `_meta`); reserve it; ensure it never materializes into task state and survives compaction/merge.
- Truncate-vs-append for uncommitted events once markers exist (uniform append may be clearer).
- `--count` direction from `--seq` (backward/older assumed) and whether SEQ itself counts.
- Behavior when SEQ is already undone, or is itself an undo event: error vs skip-and-continue.
- A future `redo` (drop the `_undoes` marker / re-apply) - out of scope, but the marker enables it; possible follow-up.
- Merge interaction: undo markers crossing branches; the merge driver should union them like other markers/removals.
- Compaction: a fully-undone event + its undo marker could both fold away once settled.
- Backward-compat: undo events already in existing logs have no `_undoes`; define how they are treated (legacy / not-undone).

RELATED: relates_to undo-diff-output (presentation). Touches action::undo (plan/apply), cli/commands/undo.rs (params/dispatch), model RESERVED keys + the `_meta`/event envelope, and possibly merge.rs + compaction. Large change - REPORT the design before building.
title: undo: rework params/semantics - keep undoing real events via an undo marker; support --seq and --seq+--count

GOAL: protect against accidental misspellings (titel, pirority) silently creating phantom columns, WITHOUT dropping schemaless or forcing a schema. Keep easy-out-of-the-box.

MODEL (soft schema / trust-on-first-use):
- The store's KNOWN VOCABULARY = every field already used by any task + declared [task_types] fields + [display] columns + status/type fields + reserved/computed names (all canonical keys).
- On create/update, BLOCK any field name not in the vocabulary unless --new-field is passed. This is the soft schema: novel columns must be introduced deliberately (once), after which they are known.
- EMPTY-STORE GRACE (Option A): while the store has ZERO tasks, the guard is dormant - the first task's fields are accepted and become the seed vocabulary. So getting started needs no --new-field; only the first task's typos can't be caught (nothing to compare to yet).
- DID-YOU-MEAN: on a block, suggest the nearest known name via Damerau-Levenshtein / OSA distance (adjacent-transposition typos titel->title, pirority->priority are distance 1), threshold scaled by length (1 short / 2 longer). Reuse the same suggestion in the closed-schema undeclared-field error.
- REDUNDANT-FLAG WARNING: if --new-field is passed but the write introduced no actually-new field name, warn (so reflexively adding --new-field everywhere nags you to stop).
- ORDER: run vet_events (incl. closed-schema enforcement) FIRST; for a CLOSED type an undeclared field is rejected by the schema (where --new-field would not help), so the guard only fires for schemaless/open types. The guard runs under the store lock (in action::write), frontend-agnostic.

- create/update: new --new-field flag.
- edit (interactive): no flag; detect new fields in preview and PROMPT - 'add these new field(s)? (no = re-edit)' - reusing the re-edit loop; pass allow_new_fields=confirmed to the write.

DONE: a global -C <DIR> / --directory <DIR> (git's -C semantics). run() set_current_dir()s into <DIR> before any store discovery or relative @FILE resolution, so any command can drive a store elsewhere. global=true (works before or after the subcommand); a bad dir is a clean "-C <dir>: <err>". e2e in tests/crud.rs (read + write via -C from an unrelated cwd; no store is created in the caller's cwd; bad-dir error). README + CLAUDE.md updated.

WHY (multi-agent arc): -C is the foundation primitive for multi-agent coordination. The git-native per-branch store RECONCILES concurrent edits (the merge driver), but can't give SYNCHRONOUS claiming across branches/machines - that needs one shared physical store. -C makes that ergonomic: from a git worktree, `ta -C ../main ...` (or a dedicated `taska`-branch worktree) drives one shared .taska as a coordination board, where the fd-lock serializes concurrent writes/claims on a single machine.

Across MACHINES there is no synchronous claim - work must be decomposed up front.

DONE. `ta undo` now walks back through real history instead of bouncing on its own compensations.

MODEL (key insight - kept the change small): a compensating undo event carries a marker `_meta.undoes=<original seq>`, but the marker only drives SELECTION, never replay. Compensations are ordinary events that already walk state back, so engine/merge/compaction are UNTOUCHED - the marker rides inside `_meta` (non-materialized, drops on compaction, no new reserved name) and `skip_serializing_if` keeps non-undo events byte-identical on disk.

DECISIONS (the two open ones were put to the user):
- Marker home: INSIDE `_meta` as `_meta:{"undoes":N}` (user's pick) - scalar per-event (matches the task's `_undoes=<seq>`), `model::UNDOES_META_KEY` + `MutationEvent::undoes`/`set_undoes`.
- Uncommitted strategy: HYBRID (user's pick) - truncate the clean uncommitted (or --remove) trailing run of selected events; append marked compensations for committed/buried ones. Preserves the clean-slate local-undo UX and all 9 prior e2e tests.
- Selection: a candidate is a non-compensation, not-already-undone event. `--seq S` starts there (must exist+be undoable, else hard error: unknown/already-undone/is-a-compensation); `--count N` walks older skipping non-candidates; no args = newest candidate.
- Targets always computed over the SURVIVING ORIGINALS (compensations dropped) so old compensations can't pin/mask a removal (this was a real bug caught in manual testing). A state-neutral (shadowed) reversal still emits an inert marker so repeated undo makes progress.

Goal: Add a new `ta watch` command that streams task mutations for tasks matching list-style filters, with debounced output similar to `ta undo`.

Specification:
- Command: `ta watch [CRITERIA...] --since SEQ`
- Filters: same as `ta list` – supports `--open`, `--ready`, and filter criteria expressions (`field=value`, etc.)
- Mandatory: `--since SEQ` – only output mutations with seq > SEQ (excluding SEQ itself)
- Optional: `--timeout TIMEOUT` – how long to block waiting for updates, default 1m55s
- Optional: `--holdout HOLDOUT` – debounce delay after first update arrives, default 10s. Accumulate updates during holdout, then output them all at once.
- Output: For each matching task that was mutated, output the updates (not full task state), consistent with `ta undo` diff format. Correctly handle text appends – only output appended text, not full field.
- Filtering: Only tasks matching the selection filter criteria are output. Only mutations since specified SEQ are considered.
- Blocking: Block for TIMEOUT duration waiting for updates. Once an update arrives, wait HOLDOUT time to accumulate more updates, then output them all.

Implementation notes:
- Reuse list filtering logic (`action::list`) for task selection
- Reuse undo-style diff rendering (`cli/commands/undo.rs` – `changed_columns`, `diff_block`, `RowStyle`)
- Need to watch the mutation log for new events (polling or inotify)
- Track last seen seq, filter events > since_seq
- Apply list filters to determine which task updates to show
- Debounce output with holdout timer
- Output format should match undo command's per-task diff with +/- markers and coloring

Open questions:
- Should watch exit after first batch (post-holdout) or continue until timeout?
- How to detect new mutations? Poll mutations.jsonl mtime / size?
- Should we support `--format json` like other output commands?
- What about deleted tasks in the filter set?

notes:
--- Approach finalized (2026-07-09) ---
Decisions:
- Cursor = seq. No head-seq echo on watch: every mutation already prints [seq:N] (commit e1f668e), so each side chains --since from its own status-transition write. Seed the first cursor with `ta status --current` (done; see status-current task).
- Compacted cursor (--since < min seq still in log): error out with a clear message, no fallback. Once-in-a-repo-lifetime; not worth a degraded path.
- Author filtering: deferred. MutationEvent has no author field, so self-trigger is handled at the PROTOCOL level (reviewer claims on wake: needs-review -> in-review owner=me, dropping the item out of its own watch set).
- Reuse: action::list filtering (compile_criteria + open/ready/criteria), engine materialize, the undo diff renderer (changed_columns/diff_block/RowStyle, cli/commands/undo.rs), FileStore locked read. Add load_mutations_since(seq) as a default method on the EventStore trait so cmd_watch stays trait-generic and the InMemory fake drives e2e. Detect changes by polling mutations.jsonl (size / last seq) with torn-read retry (reads are unlocked; read_events already skips corrupt lines).
- Holdout <= remaining timeout; updates -> exit 0, none -> "No updates yet" + exit 1. --format supported. Deleted matching task counts as an update.

OPEN FORK (confirm before building watch):
undo's diff renderer is STATE-based (before/after TaskState). The spec also wants "only appended text" for appends, but a pure before/after state diff shows the whole old+new value of an appended field, not just the delta.
  (A) State diff via undo renderer as-is: simplest reuse; appends render full old+new (violates the append clause).
  (B) Render from events with seq > since: Append -> emit only the appended payload; Update -> new value; Add/Remove -> numeric/set delta; Delete -> whole-task removal; Create -> whole task. Still routed through diff_block for identical +/- coloring.
Recommendation: (B) — event-derived deltas rendered through diff_block. A bit more code, faithful to the append clause.

Text fields diff per line (an appended note shows just that line), arrays/deps per element/edge, scalars old->new; create (before=None) is all `+`, delete (after=None) all `-`; identical states -> empty.

title: Implement 'watch' command for streaming task mutations

notes:
--- Implemented (2026-07-09) ---
`ta watch [CRITERIA...] --since SEQ [--timeout 1m55s] [--holdout 10s] [--format ...]` shipped.

Layers:
- format::state_diff (structured removed/added) + render_state_diff (colored) - shared with undo.
- action::read::rename_to_display - factored out so watch shapes at-cursor state WITHOUT timestamp/computed injection (diff shows only real mutations).
- action::list::{matching_ids, validate_criteria} - list's filter, reused; list_tasks refactored onto the shared filter_ids.
- action::watch::poll - diffs state@since vs state@now over tasks touched by events seq>since, filtered (existing on @now, deleted on @since). Compacted cursor -> error.
- cli::commands::watch::cmd_watch - poll loop (200ms), holdout debounce bounded by remaining timeout, updates->exit 0, none->"No updates yet"+exit 1. parse_duration for 1m55s/10s/etc.

Verified: 5 e2e in tests/watch.rs + parse_duration unit tests; full suite + clippy(--all-targets) + fmt green. Demoed a background watcher waking on a concurrent status flip.

Deviations from the original spec, by decision:
- No load_mutations_since trait method - load_mutations + seq filter suffices; poll is generic over EventStore for testability.
- Filters/diff use stored values, not read-time computed columns or injected timestamps (so a diff shows only real mutations); computed-column criteria won't match.
- Per-poll full materialize of both states; fine at current scale, could scope to touched tasks later if needed.
